newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet transfer value cuts Iri debt to EU level - IRI.
newsitem.headline: Stet transfer value cuts Iri debt to EU level - IRI.

text.p: The value of Italian state industry holding IRI's former stake in telecoms holding Stet has been put at 18.405 trillion lire allowing it to meet an EU deadline on debt reduction, an IRI statement said.

Iri's stake in state telecoms holding Stet which was transferred to the Treasury at the end of 1996 has been valued at 3.876 trillion lire higher than the previous 14.530 trillion minimum price estimation made in December 1996.

The Iri statement said the board of the industrial giant had met on Monday and had considered the evaluation of three advisors Giuberga Warburg, JP Morgan and brokers Albertini of the 61.27 percent of Stet ordinary capital and 0.93 percent of savings shares transferred to the Treasury in December.
The evaluators gave Stet ordinary shares a value of 7,800 lire per share and savings shares a value of 5,919 lire.
This compares with 6,792 and 4,798 respectively for the previous estimate made on the basis of market prices on December 20, 1996.

"This means the inclusion of a credit of 3.875 trillion lire from the Treasury, which brings the net debt position of IRI on June 30, 1997 to a level much lower than that stipulated as 'normal' under the (EU Commission) accord," it said.
It noted IRI also had the right to receive a further balance from the Treasury in the case of a greater value raised in the sell off of the Stet stake by the Treasury.
Stet ordinary shares were trading at 9,950 lire per share on the stock market by 0925 GMT while savings shares were at 5,920 lire.
